es: Comprender un debate público: identificar quién decide, quién se beneficia y cuál es la razón de una norma, distinguir intención de impacto y reconocer lo que se encarga a terceros (have + objeto + participio).

teaching.en: The council decides the rules, but residents are the ones who live with them.
teaching.es: El ayuntamiento decide las normas, pero los vecinos son quienes viven con ellas.
teaching.explanationEs: Quien decide y quien soporta la decisión son papeles distintos.
segments: The council decides the rules, but residents
are the ones who live with them.
teaching.audioText: The council decides the rules, but residents are the ones who live with them.

teaching.en: Shop owners, parents and cyclists are all stakeholders in the new traffic plan.
teaching.es: Comerciantes, padres y ciclistas son partes interesadas en el nuevo plan de tráfico.
teaching.explanationEs: Stakeholder: quien se ve afectado por una decisión aunque no la tome.
segments: Shop owners, parents and cyclists are all
stakeholders in the new traffic plan.
teaching.audioText: Shop owners, parents and cyclists are all stakeholders in the new traffic plan.

teaching.en: Who will benefit from the new rule, and who will pay for it?
teaching.es: ¿Quién se beneficiará de la nueva norma y quién la pagará?
teaching.explanationEs: Benefit from + norma: quien gana. Contrasta con who pays.
segments: Who will benefit from the new rule,
and who will pay for it?
teaching.audioText: Who will benefit from the new rule, and who will pay for it?

teaching.en: The rationale is simple: fewer cars mean safer streets near the school.
teaching.es: La razón de fondo es sencilla: menos coches significan calles más seguras cerca del colegio.
teaching.explanationEs: Rationale: la razón que justifica la norma; suele ir con because o so that.
segments: The rationale is simple: fewer cars
mean safer streets near the school.
teaching.audioText: The rationale is simple: fewer cars mean safer streets near the school.

teaching.en: The council argues that the ban is intended to protect children, but the impact on shops is serious.
teaching.es: El ayuntamiento sostiene que la prohibición pretende proteger a los niños, pero el impacto en los comercios es serio.
teaching.explanationEs: Intended to = la intención; impact = el efecto real, que puede ser distinto.
segments: The council argues that the ban is intended to
protect children, but the impact on shops is serious.
teaching.audioText: The council argues that the ban is intended to protect children, but the impact on shops is serious.

teaching.en: The council has the park benches painted by a contractor every spring.
teaching.es: El ayuntamiento hace que un contratista pinte los bancos del parque cada primavera.
teaching.explanationEs: Have + objeto + participio: encargas el trabajo a otro; tú no lo haces.
segments: The council has the park benches
painted by a contractor every spring.
teaching.audioText: The council has the park benches painted by a contractor every spring.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige quién toma la decisión.

choices.text: The council.
The parents.
The shop owners.

feedback.es: El verbo voted y el sujeto the council indican que el ayuntamiento es quien decide.

hint.es: El decisor es quien vota o aprueba la norma.

origin.audio: The council has voted to close Mill Street to cars during school hours.

prompt.es: Elige quién se beneficia de la norma, según el texto.

choices.text: Shop owners, because they will sell more.
Parents, because the streets will be safer.
The council, because it will earn money.

feedback.es: Los padres ganan calles más seguras; los comerciantes temen un impacto negativo y el ayuntamiento no menciona ingresos.

hint.es: Busca el grupo que recibe un efecto positivo.

origin.text: Parents welcome the ban because fewer cars mean safer streets. Shop owners fear the impact on their sales.

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Quién se beneficiará de la nueva norma?»

feedback.es: Benefit from + norma señala a quien gana con ella.

hint.es: Es el verbo que significa «beneficiarse» y va con from.

origin.text: Who will ___ from the new rule?

prompt.es: Relaciona cada papel del debate con su descripción.

feedback.es: El mayor firma la norma, los residents viven con ella, un contractor ejecuta el encargo y los stakeholders son los afectados.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué teme el comerciante.

choices.text: That accidents will increase near the school.
That the council will close his shop.
That his customers will struggle to reach the shop.

feedback.es: El comerciante apoya el objetivo, pero teme que sin aparcamiento sus clientes no lleguen a la tienda.

origin.audio: Ms Reyes, from the council: The new crossing will prevent accidents near the school. Mr Diaz, a shop owner: I agree with the aim, but parking is how my customers reach me, so the impact will be serious.

prompt.es: Completa: «La razón de la norma es proteger a los niños.»

feedback.es: Rationale es la razón de fondo que justifica una norma.

origin.text: The ___ for the rule is to protect children.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige quién sale ganando según el presidente.

choices.text: Commuters.
Residents of the street.
The bus company only.

feedback.es: El presidente afirma que los viajeros diarios se beneficiarán más; la vecina habla del impacto negativo.

origin.audio: Mr Lee, chair of the council: We will vote tonight. The bus lane is intended to cut journey times, and commuters will benefit most. Ms Park, a resident: But the impact on our street will be noise and pollution.

prompt.es: ¿Qué contraste se describe entre intención e impacto?

choices.text: The ban has reduced litter, as the mayor intended.
The ban aims to reduce litter, but it has moved the problem elsewhere.
The ban was never meant to reduce litter.

feedback.es: El alcalde pretendía reducir la basura, pero las quejas se doblaron porque el problema se trasladó a otras calles.

origin.text: The mayor says the ban is meant to reduce litter. Yet after three months, complaints have doubled because people leave rubbish in the side streets.

prompt.es: Completa: «La norma pretende proteger a los niños.»

feedback.es: Intended to + verbo expresa la intención de una norma.

origin.text: The rule is ___ to protect children.

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Quién se beneficia de la norma y quién la paga?»

answer.text: Who benefits from the rule and who pays for it

feedback.es: Benefit va con from; la pregunta separa a quien gana de quien paga.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cuál es la razón de la norma.

choices.text: To increase journey times.
To please the drivers.
To save lives on the road.

feedback.es: La razón de fondo es salvar vidas en la carretera; el aumento del tiempo de viaje es la objeción de algunos conductores.

origin.audio: Our rationale is that a lower speed limit will save lives. However, some drivers argue that it only increases journey times.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que dice que el colegio encarga la limpieza.

choices.text: The school has its windows cleaned every month.
The school cleans its windows every month.
The school has cleaned its windows by itself.

feedback.es: Have + objeto + participio indica que otro hace el trabajo; las demás opciones dicen que lo hace el propio colegio.

origin.text: Every month a cleaning company comes to wash the windows of the school. The school staff do not touch them.

prompt.es: Completa: «El ayuntamiento hace vaciar los contenedores cada lunes.»

feedback.es: Have + objeto + participio (emptied) expresa que el ayuntamiento encarga la tarea a otros.

origin.text: The council has the bins ___ every Monday.
